questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Seeing as I was only going for 4 months, I thought it would be nice to go to a country where I already spoke the language. it was important for me that the country offered interesting cultural experiences.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Even though there was a lot of information about practicality that was required before going on exhange UL was incredibly accommodating and made sure everyone was offered guidance, support and had the information they needed in time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot! University of Limerick is clearly very exchange-friendly, as they had a program for the students from the start of the exchange period. They were very aware of the challenges there can be in traveling to -and studying in a new country which they made sure to address from the start.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I could make a list of on-campus priorities. I got a room in Plassey Village - a 10 min walk from the university.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a kitchen with full cooking facilities. However, there is not much space for each person, as we were eight people and there was only two small fridges and one small freezer.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There's quite a big difference in the quality of houses. I lived in the cheapest on-campus accommodation available, and all though I don't regret choosing this, you get a bigger room, better facilities and more newly renovated accommodation If you choose another, more expensive option. Also, both on-campus, but especially off-campus is expensive! because of the housing crisis.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of steps, but UL made it fairly easy and made sure to update everyone on deadlines.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Some of the registration included online sign-up (choosing modules, providing personal info, getting the right documentation and so on). UL provided both mandatory meetings and workshops to make sure everyone registered correctly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online help as well as in-person assistance.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look for accommodation in good time. If you do not get on-campus accommodations, It can be difficult to find something. However, reach out to UL off-campus accommodation assistance - they are great help and very kind.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a greater work-load due to the amount of courses (5 compared to three at my home university). However, the courses were probably a bit easier compared to the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some required prior courses others did not.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching did not go as much into depth compared to UCPH. There was a less critical analytical approach at some of the courses and I did, to some degree, miss nuance and a more critical stance (however not all classes were pure psychology!!).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: The psychology of work, Principles of Human Resource Management, Advanced Research Methods, Developmental Psychopathology and The Sociology of Race and Racism.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely the Sociology of Race and Racism - it was pretty mind-blowing. I loved the professors approach to sociology and the quality of teaching was very high. Very interesting papers as well!.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I went traveling a lot around the country. Even though I do not regret this at all, it will cost a lot, so it is a good Idea to make a budget and  save up, if you want to go exploring. Food is also almost the same as in Denmark. Going out is cheaper though.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many great opportunities for joining clubs, going on trips with the different societies and so on. I mostly did this in the start, as I prioritized traveling with the friends I made later on, but it is such a great opportunity for exchange students to try something new out. Many of the clubs were very cheap as well.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything you can imagine. There's over 70 clubs! UL is known for its sports, so there is great facilities, even though I did not use them much. If you live on campus you also get free entrance to the gym.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I tried out Outdoor pursuits, yoga, dance and archery. I was very fond of the yoga as well as archery and outdoor pursuits. In terms of other social activities I would generally recommend going to a lot of the events organized by the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on as many trips as possible! Ireland is very beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: quite easy - Ireland is not that different from Denmark in that sense.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Joining clubs and events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I mostly just found them interesting. Ireland has a long and complicated history of being oppressed which Is still very present in the countrys cultural identity and narrative. Despite of this, they are a proud and incredibly kind and welcoming people

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How exceptionally warm, interested and welcoming everyone was. There's also a rich, musical history (irish music at most traditional pubs) which is a lot of fun! It is also one of the most politically activistic countries I have been to which I found very interesting and inspiring.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Pack for all sorts of weather
Save up 
You are bound to have a good time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: if you wan't do doing the outdoor pursuits, bring hiking boots! (they are required to go on trips).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the lovely people I got to meet, including almost every irish person. Also I really loved traveling around the country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Money!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
